A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STEER research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original entropy measurements, mathematical reasoning benchmarks, controlled interventions, and ablations in Sections 3–5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original mathematical reasoning experiments and adds coding evaluations and supplementary entropy analyses in Section 6 and Appendices C and E.

M1.justification: STEER retains GRPO and batch-normalized exponential token reweighting, but its weighting input changes: the entropy estimator replaces the (1−π)² factor with (1−π) and introduces length normalization. The probability-dependent revision changes the specified token weights. The PDFs do not establish whether this also reflects an implementation change.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates mathematical reasoning only. v2 adds code generation trained on ArcherCodeR and evaluated on LiveCodeBench v5, plus practical code editing trained on an internal corpus and evaluated on an internal held-out set and Zeta. These introduce substantially different data and task requirements.

E2.justification: Corresponding mathematical benchmark, extreme-clipping, and multi-model comparisons retain the same competitors; Cov remains the entropy-estimator comparator. New coding evaluations compare against the already-used GRPO. Edge-GRPO's added appearance in the conceptual factor table does not constitute a new evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The stated maximum training budget increases from 150 rollout steps in v1 Appendix E.2 to 200 in v2 Appendix D.2. New coding protocols use Qwen2.5-Coder 3B/7B/14B models, exact-match editing accuracy and avg@4 generation evaluation; editing permits 4096 input and 1024 output tokens. These changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of entropy continuity, dependence on model and training data, and consistency across evaluation datasets (Appendix C.1), plus clipping-threshold effects on reasoning accuracy (C.4, Table 8). Conversely, v1's Math-dataset estimator-validation plots in Figures 20–21 are removed. Existing quadrant interventions and mapping/hyperparameter ablations remain, largely relocated.

E5.justification: v1 gives no explicit independent-run counts. v2 newly reports two-run averages for main math experiments and mapping ablations, and three-run averages for coding. Neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. These disclosures do not establish an increase over v1's unspecified run counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds coding results and clipping-sweep accuracies. Existing values also change: main-table STEER AIME24 changes from 36.9 to 36.2 and its reported average from 49.1 to 48.6; SimpleRL-Zoo's average changes from 44.0 to 44.6. Extreme-scenario, additional-model, and ablation rows are revised too. STEER retains the highest math average, but changed budget and reporting descriptions preclude treating these as controlled performance differences.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and the entropy indicator receive non-equivalent probability-factor revisions. v2 Appendix F replaces the short derivation with explicit entropy-gradient and logit-update calculations and adds a remainder bound proportional to η²(Amax rmax/L)² under bounded advantages and ratios. Section 5 also introduces an inconsistent relation: λmin=exp(−α) despite α<0 and a decaying weighting function.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion extend the claimed empirical effectiveness from mathematical reasoning to both math and coding. The central contributions—explaining entropy interventions through token-level entropy change and proposing adaptive STEER reweighting—remain.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly excludes entropy-stable models and domains without verifiable rewards in Section 8, and interprets new analyses as supporting data-dependent dynamics and a stable entropy range. Most mechanism explanations remain. However, its rewritten Quadrant III paragraph says entropy increases, reversing v1's explanation and contradicting v2's own heading and diagram.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix D adds baseline-specific tuning grids and parameter values, identifies Eurus-PRIME's public-checkpoint usage, and documents coding-corpus sizes, input fields, and an ArcherCodeR access link. These substantially expand v1's generic implementation description. The STEER code link remains, but v1's blanket statement that all code and datasets accompany the supplementary material is removed.

R1.justification: v2 adds LiveCodeBench and DeepSeek-V3.2 references and removes several background citations, including Jiacai Liu's entropy derivation cited by v1's assumption and proof. Positioning against Cov and existing entropy-intervention methods remains substantially the same; most appendix related-work content is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, mechanism discussion, and method explanation are extensively rewritten. Existing-method analyses become a separate section organized around mechanisms, evidence, and limitations. Ablations move to the appendix, the proof moves to Appendix F, and an appendix contents page and dedicated limitations section are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column presentation. Clipping and sample-weighting plots are consolidated, the entropy-indicator plot is redrawn, and numerous displays move or change structure. Coding and global-entropy displays are added, Math estimator plots disappear, and estimator-statistics and extreme-scenario tables are duplicated across main text and appendices.

improvement.justification: Coding evaluations, fuller baseline settings, run-count disclosures, and explicit limitations improve coverage and transparency. However, v2 changes the central estimator without explaining how its unchanged validation numbers relate to the revision, introduces a contradictory minimum-weight parameterization, and retains outdated performance margins after updating tables. These issues affect interpretation and support for the revised method; the PDFs do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
